edges.description: Loss of the transporter reduces citrate import into neurons.
NaCT is also required in tooth-forming ameloblasts.
Intracellular citrate deficiency disrupts downstream metabolism.
Metabolic and neurotransmitter-precursor disruption dysregulates excitability.
Disrupted neuronal metabolism impairs brain development.
Elevated plasma and cerebrospinal-fluid citrate reflect failure of NaCT-mediated citrate uptake.

nodes.description: Because antiseizure medications are only partially effective, gene-replacement therapy that restores NaCT is being developed. In a preclinical model, AAV-mediated delivery of SLC13A5 rescued the epileptic and metabolic phenotypes; this is investigational and not yet an approved treatment.

evidence.reference_title: AAV-mediated gene therapy in a model of SLC13A5 citrate transporter disorder rescues epileptic and metabolic phenotypes.
evidence.snippet: AAV-mediated gene therapy in a model of SLC13A5 citrate transporter disorder  rescues epileptic and metabolic phenotypes.

nodes.description: NaCT is expressed in tooth-forming ameloblasts, where citrate contributes to enamel mineralization. Loss of NaCT impairs enamel formation, producing the characteristic dental enamel defects (amelogenesis imperfecta).

evidence.reference_title: Defective enamel and bone development in sodium-dependent citrate transporter (NaCT) Slc13a5 deficient mice.
evidence.snippet: Slc13a5 deficiency led to defective tooth development,  characterized by absence of mature enamel, formation of aberrant enamel matrix,  and dysplasia and hyperplasia of the enamel organ epithelium that progressed  with age.

nodes.description: Intracellular citrate is a metabolic hub: it feeds the tricarboxylic acid cycle, provides carbon for acetyl-CoA, and supplies precursors for neurotransmitter (glutamate and GABA) synthesis. Its deficiency disrupts neuronal energy metabolism and neurotransmitter precursor supply.

evidence.reference_title: Role of sodium dependent SLC13 transporter inhibitors in various metabolic disorders.
evidence.snippet: Citrate in the cytosol works as a precursor for  the fatty acid synthesis, cholesterol, and low-density lipoproteins.

evidence.reference_title: Role of sodium dependent SLC13 transporter inhibitors in various metabolic disorders.
evidence.snippet: controls the energy balance by  downregulating the glycolysis, tricarboxylic acid (TCA), and fatty acid  breakdown.

evidence.snippet: loss of SLC13A5 function  alters tricarboxylic acid cycle (TCA) metabolism and may disrupt metabolic  compartmentation in the brain.

evidence.snippet: Distinctive elevations of citrate and dysregulation of citric acid  cycle intermediates, supporting the hypothesis that loss of SLC13A5 function  alters tricarboxylic acid cycle (TCA) metabolism

nodes.description: Disrupted neuronal energy and biosynthetic metabolism impairs neuronal maturation and brain development, producing developmental delay and intellectual disability.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in SLC13A5 cause autosomal-recessive epileptic encephalopathy with seizure onset in the first days of life.
evidence.snippet: profound  developmental delay with no facial dysmorphism.

nodes.description: With NaCT deficient, neurons cannot efficiently take up extracellular citrate, so intracellular citrate is reduced while extracellular and cerebrospinal-fluid citrate accumulate.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in SLC13A5 cause autosomal-recessive epileptic encephalopathy with seizure onset in the first days of life.
evidence.snippet: SLC13A5, which encodes the cytoplasmic sodium-dependent citrate carrier, notably  expressed in neurons.

evidence.reference_title: Recessive mutations in SLC13A5 result in a loss of citrate transport and cause neonatal epilepsy, developmental delay and teeth hypoplasia.
evidence.snippet: Neurons are considered incapable of de novo synthesis of  tricarboxylic acid cycle intermediates; therefore they rely on the uptake of  intermediates, such as citrate, to maintain their energy status and  neurotransmitter production.

nodes.description: Biallelic loss-of-function variants in SLC13A5 abolish or reduce the activity of NaCT, the plasma-membrane sodium-dependent citrate transporter that imports extracellular citrate into cells.

evidence.snippet: Mutations  affected key residues for sodium binding, which is critical for citrate  transport.

nodes.description: Disrupted citrate-dependent metabolism, altered neurotransmitter precursor supply, and possibly altered extracellular citrate chelation of the divalent cations that modulate NMDA receptors dysregulate neuronal excitability, producing hyperexcitability and seizures.
